title: Excel Sheet Column Title
summary: Given an integer columnNumber, generate its equivalent column title as it would appear in an Excel sheet.
statement: Given an integer columnNumber, generate its equivalent column title as it would appear in an Excel sheet. For instance, 1 corresponds to A, 2 to B, 26 to Z, 27 to AA, and 28 to AB.
constraints: Use uppercase column labels with A=1, …, Z=26, AA=27, AB=28. There is no zero-valued letter; return the label as a string.
hints: Column letters represent digits 1 through 26, not 0 through 25.
Subtract one before taking a remainder so the final letter maps to A through Z.
Repeatedly divide number-1 by 26; append the remainder's letter and continue with the quotient; reverse at the end.
At 26, the last letter is Z and the remaining quotient must be zero, not one.
editorial: Subtracting one converts the current one-based digit into a zero-based remainder. Each division removes the final letter, so reverse the collected letters when finished. The independent oracle first locates the block of labels with a given length, then unranks the number within that block using ordinary positional base 26. The opposite conversion is a separate input/output contract, not a duplicate of this problem.

tests.explanation: Column 1 is A, the first single-letter label.
After Z (26) comes AA (27), then AB (28). This is not ordinary base 26 with A equal to zero.
